title: Nine vanishing transients on 1950s plates, follow-up with Gran Telescopio Canarias
place_text: Palomar Sky Survey plates; Gran Telescopio Canarias, Canary Islands

tellings.quote: Uh we had this guy at Grand Telescope Canaria, one of my friends who actually pointed the world's largest optical telescope, a 10.4 m telescope to the positions of all these nine objects or eight of them or something like that and there was nothing left.

plain: Nine points of light that show up on photographs of the sky from the 1950s Palomar Sky Survey, a photographic map of the whole sky, are now gone: a friend of the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel pointed the Gran Telescopio Canarias, a 10.4-metre telescope in the Canary Islands and the world's largest optical telescope, at "all these nine objects or eight of them" and "there was nothing left." Villarroel tells Michels this as her own work and mentions a US Navy star catalogue alongside the old images. If the objects were real, something bright was in those spots in the 1950s and has since disappeared.
